title: National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) conducts sixth outreach programmes with focus on small and medium auditors under the theme “Creating a Better Financial Reporting Ecosystem” in Ahmedabad, today
subtitle: The outreach aims to support professional capacity, strengthen audit quality and improve the quality of financial reporting
body_text:
The National Financial Reporting Authority (NFRA) completed its sixth outreach programme at Ahmedabad recently, in a series of outreach programmes that commenced in 2025. The  programme with the theme “Creating a Better Financial Reporting Ecosystem”, was inaugurated by Nitin Gupta, Chairperson, NFRA and CA Prasanna Kumar D, President, of ICAI.
With the focus on small and medium auditors and an aim to support in professional capacity, strengthen audit quality and improve the quality of financial reporting, this was the second such outreach programme held in collaboration with the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India (ICAI), the first being at Pune in June 2026.
Shri Nitin Gupta, Chairperson, NFRA, in his keynote address, emphasised the pivotal role of the accountancy profession in safeguarding public interest and building trust in financial reporting. Shri Gupta emphasised the need to remain aligned with contemporary global standards and called upon the audit firms to continuously enhance their competencies, including adopting appropriate technology in the audit process.
In his address, CA Prasanna Kumar D, President ICAI, stated that audit quality in financial reporting is critical for building trust and confidence among the stakeholders.
Ms Smita Jhingran, Full-Time Member, NFRA, highlighted the importance of NFRA's inspection of audit firms in ensuring high-quality financial reporting.
The experts’ sessions aimed at providing practical insights for improving audit quality in day-to-day professional work and comprised technical sessions on key aspects such as Audit Strategy Documentation, Risk of Material Mis-statements, and case studies on takeaways from NFRA's oversight.
Since this initiative was launched last year, NFRA’s outreach programmes have elicited participation from representatives of more than 450 small and medium firms.

enrichment.summary: NFRA held its sixth outreach programme, in Ahmedabad, focused on small and medium auditors under the theme 'Creating a Better Financial Reporting Ecosystem'. It was the second such programme conducted jointly with ICAI, following one in Pune in June 2026, and featured technical sessions on audit strategy, risk of material misstatements, and NFRA oversight case studies. Since the initiative began in 2025, over 450 small and medium audit firms have participated.
enrichment.context: NFRA is India's independent audit regulator, established under the Companies Act, 2013 following the collapse of large corporate frauds (like IL&FS and PMC Bank), replacing the earlier self-regulatory mechanism of ICAI for certain classes of companies. It monitors compliance with accounting and auditing standards, investigates professional misconduct by auditors, and has powers to penalize erring chartered accountants and audit firms. These outreach programmes represent NFRA's capacity-building efforts aimed at small and medium audit practitioners who often lack resources to keep pace with evolving standards, in contrast to NFRA's more adversarial regulatory/enforcement role against large firms. This event is routine institutional capacity-building activity with no new policy or regulatory announcement.
